subject: Lifecycle profiles + region selectors: roadmap request & ops runbook
messages:
From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@nimbusp ay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mapping tenant lifecycle to region selectors — quick Q

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope the integration:

- We need to offer customers per-tenant "lifecycle profiles" (e.g., 30-day dev, 365-day standard, indefinite legal-hold) and be able to pin the storage region per profile.
- We want to be able to rollback a delete within a short window (soft-delete / restore) for the standard profile, but for legal-hold profiles deletes must be blocked and audited.
- For some EU tenants we need to ensure data is physically stored in eu-west-1 and have an auditable deletion chain for compliance reviews.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports: 1) per-tenant lifecycle + region selection via API, 2) soft-delete windows by profile, and 3) a legal-hold flag that prevents purge? If not, what would the implementation roadmap look like and what are the engineering constraints?

Attached is a spreadsheet with examples of the profiles we're considering.

Thanks,
Taylor
Taylor Nguyen
Head of Data Ops, NimbusPay
(taylor@nimbusp ay.com)

Attachment: nimbus-retention-examples.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@nimbusp ay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping tenant lifecycle to region selectors — quick Q

Hi Taylor — thanks for the clear examples, and for flagging the EU constraint. Quick answers up front: 1) Not today as a single API surface (we have per-workspace defaults + region placement policies), 2) we have a soft-delete concept in our internal roadmap but not profile-driven yet, 3) legal-hold is supported in a limited way (account-level hold via support).

I'm looping in Karthik to outline feasibility and a proposed incremental roadmap that covers: profile API, region selector binding, soft-delete window enforcement, and explicit legal-hold that integrates with audit logs.

Can you confirm the SLAs you need for rollback (e.g., restore within 72 hrs vs 30 days) and whether the legal team needs immutable storage guarantees (WORM) or just administrative block + audit trail? That will shape the design.

Thanks — I'll put together a short ops/runbook draft and timeline for engineering.

Best,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance PM, Redwood Inference
(irene@redwoodinference.com)

Attachment: profile-diff-20260621.csv

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@nimbusp ay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping tenant lifecycle to region selectors — quick Q

Hi Irene,

Thanks — for NimbusPay the important bits are:
- Restore window: 7 days for standard profiles (we can automate shorter windows later).
- Legal-hold: administrative block + tamper-evident audit trail is sufficient; we don't need WORM unless it's an explicit regulatory requirement for a subset of customers.
- EU tenants: physical locality is a hard requirement (eu-west-1). For cross-region replication we need a consent/flag per-tenant — some customers will allow it, some will not.

Also looping in our counsel: priya@legal-nimbus.com for any legal nuance.

Taylor

Subject: Re: Mapping tenant lifecycle to region selectors — quick Q

Hi all — thanks Taylor for the detail. A few engineering notes and a suggested incremental plan: 

Notes:
- Current state: we support per-workspace region placement and a global retention policy with manual interventions for legal holds. No per-tenant lifecycle API today.
- Constraints: physical-region guarantees add scheduling and capacity implications (we currently autoscale across zones/regions for efficiency). Pinning requires a placement affinity layer and capacity reservations for Dedicated customers.
- Soft-delete: feasible to implement with a tombstone + delayed purge pipeline; complexity is moderate and interacts with backup/replication code paths.
- Legal-hold: easiest path is an admin flag that prevents the purge pipeline from deleting records and surfaces hold reasons in the audit log. Immutable-WORM requires storage-provider support (we would rely on partner cloud features).

Proposed incremental roadmap: 
1) MVP (6–8 weeks): profile schema + admin API to attach a region selector and retention window to a tenant. Soft-delete TTL implemented as a purge queue with configurable delay.
2) Week 9–12: audit log surface + legal-hold admin flag (prevents purge). Integrations with existing observability and console.
3) Quarter 2 follow-up: capacity reservation patterns for pinned-region Dedicated customers and an optional WORM-backed profile for regulated tenants.

Operational asks for NimbusPay before we commit timeline: 
- Prioritized list of sample tenants and which profile/region combo they need.
- Expected QPS/volume per tenant (region pinning affects capacity planning).
- Acceptance criteria for restore (e.g., success & verification steps).

Marissa — from a commercial perspective we should capture any contractual language (SLA for restore window, region residency guarantee) before engineering work begins.

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

- Contract language: "region residency" must be scoped to the tenant IDs and to the retention profiles that opt into pinning; also we need to define restore SLA (7-day window) and legal-hold process (admin request + audit log export).
